opening.text: Stand at the end of a high diving board and look down. Your knees feel soft. Your heart pounds. Everyone knows the feeling. Courage is not the lack of that feeling. It is stepping off anyway. And almost always, the fall is shorter than we feared.

mainMessage.text: Courage is stepping off the board while afraid, trusting that God is with us.

blocks.text: **The call comes to all** Every one of us stands on some board. Fear comes to everyone.
Have not I commanded thee? Be strong and of a good courage; be not afraid, neither be thou dismayed: for the Lord thy God is with thee whithersoever thou goest.
President Thomas S. Monson, President of the Church, said this in his talk “Be Strong and of a Good Courage” from the April 2014 general conference.
The call for courage comes constantly to each of us.
The call comes to all.
**Faith and courage together** Courage and faith lift each other. Disciples need both.
Be strong and of a good courage, fear not, nor be afraid of them: for the Lord thy God, he it is that doth go with thee; he will not fail thee, nor forsake thee.
Elder Neil L. Andersen of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Courage Born of Our Faith in Jesus Christ” from the October 2026 general conference.
Faith and courage are hallmarks of disciples of Jesus Christ.
Faith and courage go together.
**Right over easy** The easy way is the shallow end. The right way is the deep one.

If it be so, our God whom we serve is able to deliver us from the burning fiery furnace, and he will deliver us out of thine hand, O king. But if not, be it known unto thee, O king, that we will not serve thy gods, nor worship the golden image which thou hast set up.
President Thomas S. Monson, President of the Church, said this in his talk “Be Strong and of a Good Courage” from the April 2014 general conference.
Courage, not compromise, brings the smile of God’s approval.
Choose the right.
**Every day, a small board** Most days, we don't need to jump off cliffs. We face small moments that need a little courage.
Fear thou not; for I am with thee: be not dismayed; for I am thy God: I will strengthen thee; yea, I will help thee; yea, I will uphold thee with the right hand of my righteousness.
Sister Ann M. Dibb, Second Counselor in the Young Women General Presidency, said this in her talk “Be of a Good Courage” from the April 2010 general conference.
We are faced every day with situations that require courage and strength.
Small boards, every day.
**Winning over fear** Courage doesn't skip the fear. It wins over it, one step at a time.
For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.
Elder Neil L. Andersen of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Courage Born of Our Faith in Jesus Christ” from the October 2026 general conference.
Spiritual courage is the triumph over obstacles, doubt, and fear in choosing the right.
Win over fear.
**Stand when others sit** Sometimes courage looks like standing alone. We stand for what is right.
Then Peter and the other apostles answered and said, We ought to obey God rather than men.
President Thomas S. Monson, President of the Church, said this in his talk “Be Strong and of a Good Courage” from the April 2014 general conference.
Let us—all of us—have the courage to defy the consensus, the courage to stand for principle.
Stand for principle.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they did something brave, even a small thing. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: David and Goliath

blocks.text: A giant had frightened the whole army. A young shepherd stepped forward.

David said moreover, The Lord that delivered me out of the paw of the lion, and out of the paw of the bear, he will deliver me out of the hand of this Philistine. And Saul said unto David, Go, and the Lord be with thee. Then said David to the Philistine, Thou comest to me with a sword, and with a spear, and with a shield: but I come to thee in the name of the Lord of hosts, the God of the armies of Israel, whom thou hast defied.
David remembered what God had already done for him. That memory gave him courage. We can remember the same.

application.text: First, name one thing you have been afraid to do that is right. Second, ask Heavenly Father for the courage to take the first step. Third, take it this week.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know Heavenly Father is with us when we are afraid. I know Jesus Christ was the bravest of all. I know courage grows each time we choose the right. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

opening.text: A flagpole in a strong wind doesn't bend over and hide. The flag whips and snaps. But the pole stands. It was set deep in the ground. Courage is like that pole. The wind will blow. What matters is how deep we are set.

mainMessage.text: Courage is standing firm in the wind because we are set deep in the Lord.

blocks.text: **The wind always comes** Nobody gets through life without wind. The call to be brave is ongoing.
Have not I commanded thee? Be strong and of a good courage; be not afraid, neither be thou dismayed: for the Lord thy God is with thee whithersoever thou goest.
President Thomas S. Monson, President of the Church, said this in his talk “Be Strong and of a Good Courage” from the April 2014 general conference.
The call for courage comes constantly to each of us.
The wind comes.
**Set in faith** The pole is set in the ground. We are set in faith, and faith and courage grow together.
Be strong and of a good courage, fear not, nor be afraid of them: for the Lord thy God, he it is that doth go with thee; he will not fail thee, nor forsake thee.
Elder Neil L. Andersen of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Courage Born of Our Faith in Jesus Christ” from the October 2026 general conference.
Faith and courage are hallmarks of disciples of Jesus Christ.
Stay set.
**Not bending to the gust** A pole that bends to every gust will break. Courage doesn't bend to what is popular.

If it be so, our God whom we serve is able to deliver us from the burning fiery furnace, and he will deliver us out of thine hand, O king. But if not, be it known unto thee, O king, that we will not serve thy gods, nor worship the golden image which thou hast set up.
President Thomas S. Monson, President of the Church, said this in his talk “Be Strong and of a Good Courage” from the April 2014 general conference.
Courage, not compromise, brings the smile of God’s approval.
Don't bend.
**A breeze every day** Most winds are small. We build courage in the little gusts.
Fear thou not; for I am with thee: be not dismayed; for I am thy God: I will strengthen thee; yea, I will help thee; yea, I will uphold thee with the right hand of my righteousness.
Sister Ann M. Dibb, Second Counselor in the Young Women General Presidency, said this in her talk “Be of a Good Courage” from the April 2010 general conference.
We are faced every day with situations that require courage and strength.
Practice in the small gusts.
**Fear rattles, faith holds** The rope rattles in the wind. That doesn't mean the pole is falling. Courage wins over fear.
For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.
Elder Neil L. Andersen of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Courage Born of Our Faith in Jesus Christ” from the October 2026 general conference.
Spiritual courage is the triumph over obstacles, doubt, and fear in choosing the right.
Faith holds.
**A flag for others to see** A flag lets others know where we stand. Our courage can show others what is right.
Then Peter and the other apostles answered and said, We ought to obey God rather than men.
President Thomas S. Monson, President of the Church, said this in his talk “Be Strong and of a Good Courage” from the April 2014 general conference.
Let us—all of us—have the courage to defy the consensus, the courage to stand for principle.
Show where you stand.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they stood up for what was right. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Esther goes to the king

blocks.text: Esther's people were in danger. Going to the king uninvited could cost her life.

For if thou altogether holdest thy peace at this time, then shall there enlargement and deliverance arise to the Jews from another place; but thou and thy father’s house shall be destroyed: and who knoweth whether thou art come to the kingdom for such a time as this? Go, gather together all the Jews that are present in Shushan, and fast ye for me, and neither eat nor drink three days, night or day: I also and my maidens will fast likewise; and so will I go in unto the king, which is not according to the law: and if I perish, I perish.
Esther fasted and prayed with her people first. Then she went. Courage was born of faith and preparation.

application.text: First, think of a place where you've been quiet about what you believe. Second, pray for the words and the courage to speak kindly. Third, say one honest, gentle thing.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know Heavenly Father holds us steady. I know Jesus Christ is with us in the wind. I know courage grows when we trust Him. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

opening.text: Carry a lantern through a dark house at night. You can't see the whole house. You see only a few steps ahead. But those steps are lit. And when you take them, the next few light up. Courage often works this way. We don't see everything. We see enough for the next step.

mainMessage.text: Courage is taking the next lit step, trusting God for the rest.

blocks.text: **Everyone walks in the dark sometimes** No one escapes dark rooms. The call to be brave keeps coming.
Have not I commanded thee? Be strong and of a good courage; be not afraid, neither be thou dismayed: for the Lord thy God is with thee whithersoever thou goest.
President Thomas S. Monson, President of the Church, said this in his talk “Be Strong and of a Good Courage” from the April 2014 general conference.
The call for courage comes constantly to each of us.
The dark rooms come.
**The lantern is faith** Faith is the light we carry. Courage walks by it.
Be strong and of a good courage, fear not, nor be afraid of them: for the Lord thy God, he it is that doth go with thee; he will not fail thee, nor forsake thee.
Elder Neil L. Andersen of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Courage Born of Our Faith in Jesus Christ” from the October 2026 general conference.
Faith and courage are hallmarks of disciples of Jesus Christ.
Carry the light.
**Not the brighter, easier hall** There may be a bright hall that leads the wrong way. Courage takes the right door, even when it's dim.

If it be so, our God whom we serve is able to deliver us from the burning fiery furnace, and he will deliver us out of thine hand, O king. But if not, be it known unto thee, O king, that we will not serve thy gods, nor worship the golden image which thou hast set up.
President Thomas S. Monson, President of the Church, said this in his talk “Be Strong and of a Good Courage” from the April 2014 general conference.
Courage, not compromise, brings the smile of God’s approval.
Take the right door.
**Steps in ordinary rooms** Most of our walking is in ordinary rooms. That's where courage is built.
Fear thou not; for I am with thee: be not dismayed; for I am thy God: I will strengthen thee; yea, I will help thee; yea, I will uphold thee with the right hand of my righteousness.
Sister Ann M. Dibb, Second Counselor in the Young Women General Presidency, said this in her talk “Be of a Good Courage” from the April 2010 general conference.
We are faced every day with situations that require courage and strength.
Ordinary rooms, daily steps.
**Shadows aren't monsters** In the dark, a coat on a chair looks like a figure. Fear makes shadows bigger. Courage looks closer.
For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.
Elder Neil L. Andersen of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Courage Born of Our Faith in Jesus Christ” from the October 2026 general conference.
Spiritual courage is the triumph over obstacles, doubt, and fear in choosing the right.
Look closer.
**Holding the light for others** Others are walking in the dark too. When we stand for what is right, our light helps them.
Then Peter and the other apostles answered and said, We ought to obey God rather than men.
President Thomas S. Monson, President of the Church, said this in his talk “Be Strong and of a Good Courage” from the April 2014 general conference.
Let us—all of us—have the courage to defy the consensus, the courage to stand for principle.
Light the way.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they walked ahead without seeing it all. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: The young warriors

blocks.text: Two thousand young men had never fought a battle. They went anyway.

And they were all young men, and they were exceedingly valiant for courage, and also for strength and activity; but behold, this was not all—they were men who were true at all times in whatsoever thing they were entrusted. Now they never had fought, yet they did not fear death; and they did think more upon the liberty of their fathers than they did upon their lives; yea, they had been taught by their mothers, that if they did not doubt, God would deliver them.
Their courage came from what they had been taught at home. Their mothers lit the lantern first.

application.text: First, think of a choice ahead that you can't see all the way through. Second, pray and ask what the next step is. Third, take that step and trust the light for the next one.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know Heavenly Father lights the next step. I know Jesus Christ walks with us in dark rooms. I know faith turns fear into courage. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

opening.text: A hiker on a steep trail doesn't walk alone if she's wise. She hires a guide who knows the path. The guide says, "Step here. Not there." The hiker still has to climb. But she isn't guessing. Courage is climbing with the One who knows the way.

mainMessage.text: Courage is climbing the steep trail with a guide who has been there before.

blocks.text: **The trail is steep for all** Every person climbs something hard. The call to be brave never stops.
Have not I commanded thee? Be strong and of a good courage; be not afraid, neither be thou dismayed: for the Lord thy God is with thee whithersoever thou goest.
President Thomas S. Monson, President of the Church, said this in his talk “Be Strong and of a Good Courage” from the April 2014 general conference.
The call for courage comes constantly to each of us.
The trail is steep.
**Trust the guide** We trust the guide because we have faith in Him. Faith and courage grow side by side.
Be strong and of a good courage, fear not, nor be afraid of them: for the Lord thy God, he it is that doth go with thee; he will not fail thee, nor forsake thee.
Elder Neil L. Andersen of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Courage Born of Our Faith in Jesus Christ” from the October 2026 general conference.
Faith and courage are hallmarks of disciples of Jesus Christ.
Trust the guide.
**The shortcut is a cliff** There's often a shortcut. It looks easier. A good guide says no. Courage follows the guide.

If it be so, our God whom we serve is able to deliver us from the burning fiery furnace, and he will deliver us out of thine hand, O king. But if not, be it known unto thee, O king, that we will not serve thy gods, nor worship the golden image which thou hast set up.
President Thomas S. Monson, President of the Church, said this in his talk “Be Strong and of a Good Courage” from the April 2014 general conference.
Courage, not compromise, brings the smile of God’s approval.
Skip the shortcut.
**One switchback at a time** Nobody climbs a mountain in one move. We climb one switchback at a time, every day.
Fear thou not; for I am with thee: be not dismayed; for I am thy God: I will strengthen thee; yea, I will help thee; yea, I will uphold thee with the right hand of my righteousness.
Sister Ann M. Dibb, Second Counselor in the Young Women General Presidency, said this in her talk “Be of a Good Courage” from the April 2010 general conference.
We are faced every day with situations that require courage and strength.
One turn at a time.
**Looking down** The fear of heights hits when we look down. The guide says, "Look at the next step." Courage wins over fear that way.
For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.
Elder Neil L. Andersen of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Courage Born of Our Faith in Jesus Christ” from the October 2026 general conference.
Spiritual courage is the triumph over obstacles, doubt, and fear in choosing the right.
Look at the next step.
**Climbing in a group** Other climbers watch how we go. When one stands firm, others find their footing.
Then Peter and the other apostles answered and said, We ought to obey God rather than men.
President Thomas S. Monson, President of the Church, said this in his talk “Be Strong and of a Good Courage” from the April 2014 general conference.
Let us—all of us—have the courage to defy the consensus, the courage to stand for principle.
Give others footing.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they did a hard thing because they trusted God. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Nephi returns for the plates

blocks.text: Nephi's brothers wanted to quit. Nephi chose to go back.

And it came to pass that I, Nephi, said unto my father: I will go and do the things which the Lord hath commanded, for I know that the Lord giveth no commandments unto the children of men, save he shall prepare a way for them that they may accomplish the thing which he commandeth them.
Nephi didn't know the way. He knew the Guide. That was enough to begin.

application.text: First, pick one hard thing God has asked of you. Second, ask Him to show you the next step, not the whole path. Third, take that step before the week ends.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know Jesus Christ knows the way because He walked it. I know He prepares a way for what He asks. I know we are never climbing alone. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

opening.text: A seed under the ground has a hard job. It has to push up through heavy soil. It can't see the sun. It just pushes. And one day it breaks through. Courage is like that seed. It pushes toward the light, even when the soil feels heavy.

mainMessage.text: Courage is pushing toward the light, one small inch at a time.

blocks.text: **The soil is heavy for everyone** Every seed meets hard ground. We all meet things that press on us.
Have not I commanded thee? Be strong and of a good courage; be not afraid, neither be thou dismayed: for the Lord thy God is with thee whithersoever thou goest.
President Thomas S. Monson, President of the Church, said this in his talk “Be Strong and of a Good Courage” from the April 2014 general conference.
The call for courage comes constantly to each of us.
The call comes to all.
**Roots of faith** A seed needs roots. Our courage needs roots too. Faith feeds it.
Be strong and of a good courage, fear not, nor be afraid of them: for the Lord thy God, he it is that doth go with thee; he will not fail thee, nor forsake thee.
Elder Neil L. Andersen of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Courage Born of Our Faith in Jesus Christ” from the October 2026 general conference.
Faith and courage are hallmarks of disciples of Jesus Christ.
Feed the roots.
**Growing toward the right light** A plant grows toward the light, not toward the easy shade. Courage grows toward what is right.

If it be so, our God whom we serve is able to deliver us from the burning fiery furnace, and he will deliver us out of thine hand, O king. But if not, be it known unto thee, O king, that we will not serve thy gods, nor worship the golden image which thou hast set up.
President Thomas S. Monson, President of the Church, said this in his talk “Be Strong and of a Good Courage” from the April 2014 general conference.
Courage, not compromise, brings the smile of God’s approval.
Grow toward the light.
**Small growth, every day** You can't watch a seed grow. But it grows every day. Our courage grows in small daily choices.
Fear thou not; for I am with thee: be not dismayed; for I am thy God: I will strengthen thee; yea, I will help thee; yea, I will uphold thee with the right hand of my righteousness.
Sister Ann M. Dibb, Second Counselor in the Young Women General Presidency, said this in her talk “Be of a Good Courage” from the April 2010 general conference.
We are faced every day with situations that require courage and strength.
Grow a little each day.
**Through the frost** Frost comes. A seedling that stays rooted survives it. Courage wins over fear by staying rooted.
For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.
Elder Neil L. Andersen of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Courage Born of Our Faith in Jesus Christ” from the October 2026 general conference.
Spiritual courage is the triumph over obstacles, doubt, and fear in choosing the right.
Stay rooted.
**A tree that shades others** One day the seedling is a tree. Others rest in its shade. Our courage can become shelter for someone else.
Then Peter and the other apostles answered and said, We ought to obey God rather than men.
President Thomas S. Monson, President of the Church, said this in his talk “Be Strong and of a Good Courage” from the April 2014 general conference.
Let us—all of us—have the courage to defy the consensus, the courage to stand for principle.
Be a shelter.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when their courage helped someone else. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Caleb says go up

blocks.text: Ten spies came back afraid. Caleb and Joshua said the land could be taken.

And Caleb stilled the people before Moses, and said, Let us go up at once, and possess it; for we are well able to overcome it. Only rebel not ye against the Lord, neither fear ye the people of the land; for they are bread for us: their defence is departed from them, and the Lord is with us: fear them not.
Caleb stood almost alone. He said, "the Lord is with us." One steady voice can calm a whole crowd.

application.text: First, notice where fear is keeping you small. Second, ask the Lord to strengthen your roots through prayer and scripture. Third, do one brave, right thing this week, and let someone see it.

blocks.text: I know Heavenly Father gives us power, love and a sound mind. I know Jesus Christ makes our courage grow. I know the Lord is with us. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.
